name: MedSynthDetect: A Real vs AI-Generated Medical Image Dataset of X-ray, CT and MRI
description: This dataset is designed for detecting AI-generated (synthetic) medical images. It contains real and AI-generated images from three imaging modalities: X-ray, computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The real images were collected between February and April 2025 from publically available data source. The AI-generated images were created with ChatGPT using text prompts that ask for realistic medical scans of each modality. A student of the DIU NLP & ML Research Lab, Daffodil International University, prepared the dataset under the supervision of the lab's supervisors. The dataset is organised into six folders: X-ray: real X-ray images (500) AI_X-ray: ChatGPT-generated X-ray images (500) CT Scan: real CT images (500) AI_CT Scan: ChatGPT-generated CT images (500) MRI: real MRI images ([496]) AI_MRI: ChatGPT-generated MRI images ([385]) Images in each folder are numbered sequentially (1, 2, 3, …). All images were resized to 512×512 pixels and saved in PNG format, so that file format and resolution do not reveal whether an image is real or synthetic. Exact duplicate images were removed. All patient-identifying information was removed from the real images. The dataset supports binary real-vs-fake classification, six-class classification (modality × authenticity), cross-modality generalisation studies (for example, training on X-ray and testing on MRI), and benchmarking of deepfake and synthetic-image detectors in medical imaging. With generative AI tools now widely available, fabricated medical images are a risk to clinical trust, insurance and research integrity. This dataset gives researchers a starting point for building detectors against this kind of misuse. The synthetic images are not clinically valid and must not be used for diagnosis.
